newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - up as new issues sell well.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - up as new issues sell well.

text.p: U.S. municipal bond prices were up about 1/4 to 3/8 point at the close as the market successfully fought off the day's heavy new issue calendar, traders said.

Reception to the roughly $1.3 billion of new issue pricings was strong, with the account already closed on the largest deal of the day, a $201.3 million Lower Colorado River Authority, Texas's $201.3 million competitive issue.
Merrill Lynch & Co, which won the deal, reoffered the 2012 maturity at 5.30 percent. To see the pricing scale, double click on double click on nN20280834.
In negotiated action, PaineWebber Inc said it repriced Triborough Bridge and Tunnel Authority, N.Y.'s $201 million revenue bond deal.
The firm was able to cut yields five basis points in several maturities and dropped the top yield in 2027 to 5.60 percent from 5.65 percent. To see the repricing scale, double click on nN2045960.
Bear Stearns & Co was also able to raise prices on several maturities of a $140.8 million Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development revenue bond issue.
It left the top yield in 2028 unchanged at 5.95 percent. To see the repricing scale, double click on nN2043554.
In the muni secondary, bids on Chicago Skyway 5-1/2s of 2023 were unchanged late Wednesday at 5.76 percent, after being quoted up two basis points earlier in the day.
Texas Turnpike Authority 5-1/4s of 2023 were two basis points lower at 5.57 percent net. Those bonds were quoted up one basis point earlier at midday.
In debt futures, the December municipal contract finished at 117-22/32, up 18/32.
December T-bonds were up 16/32 to 115-23/32, widening the MOB spread to 63 ticks from 61 ticks at the close Tuesday.
Thursday's scheduled competitive and negotiated municipal bond sales are expected to total $311 million in 24 offerings, according to Reuters Municipal Bond Information Group.
Competitive sales total $131.7 million in 13 issues. The largest is a $40 million Clark County School District, Nev., deal at 1230 EST.
Negotiated sales total $179 million in 11 offerings. The largest is a $35 million California Health Facilities Authority deal through PaineWebber Inc.
